page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.32xlarge is an enterprise-grade general purpose virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by the AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 128 dedicated vCPUs, delivering high-density multi-threaded compute capability without resource contention from shared-core virtualization.

System memory totals 512 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4 GB per virtual core. The instance provides no integrated local disk storage, requiring external cloud block storage for persistent filesystems and data volumes. Network performance is provisioned with a 40 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the hardware profile includes zero GPU accelerators.

The 1:4 memory balance and 128-core density offer cost-efficient consolidation for scale-up multi-threaded workloads, eliminating the premium overhead of GPU-accelerated or memory-skewed instances. Because local NVMe is omitted, I/O intensive databases depend directly on remote storage performance. This server is suitable for large-scale enterprise applications, high-concurrency web serving, distributed batch processing, and container cluster worker nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8a.32xlarge is an enterprise-class general purpose instance powered by a 2.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9T24 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Provisioned through the KVM hypervisor, it features 128 dedicated vCPUs and 512 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory allocation of 4 GB per vCPU. The server includes no local disk storage, relying on attached cloud storage solutions for persistent data, and does not incorporate dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a 40 Gbps baseline bandwidth. With its high core density and balanced memory allocation, the instance delivers efficient multi-core processing without paying a premium for specialized hardware accelerators. The ecs.g8a.32xlarge is suitable for enterprise application backends, container orchestration nodes, large distributed data processing jobs, and high-traffic web server deployments.
